summary.headline: Hindalco Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 58% YoY to INR13,481 crore and PAT 75% to INR7,013 crore, led by record India upstream EBITDA of INR7,390 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated business segment EBITDA rose 58% YoY to INR13,481 crore and PAT rose 75% to INR7,013 crore, with Hindalco India EBITDA up 73% to INR8,606 crore. India upstream aluminium posted a record INR7,390 crore EBITDA (USD2,331/t, 55% margin) on higher LME and favourable macros, while copper delivered a record INR918 crore despite a planned smelter shutdown. Novelis volumes fell 5% YoY to 916 kt and adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to USD516 million, but the Oswego fire outage and elevated US tariffs (USD70 million) weighed on the quarter. Management guided volumes higher in Q2 for downstream aluminium and copper, and said sulphuric acid prices will stay near Q1 levels in Q2.

segments.name: India upstream aluminium
segments.commentary: Shipments up 3% YoY and revenue up 44% YoY; record EBITDA of INR7,390 crore. Hedged about 29% of FY27 aluminium at USD3,004/t and 18% of FX at INR91.63/USD.

segments.name: India downstream aluminium
segments.commentary: Shipments up 3% YoY to 104 kt; EBITDA INR298 crore, up 30%, on volume, mix and premiumisation. Management sees a sustainable downstream margin nearer USD250/t than the USD300 seen in Q1.

segments.name: India copper
segments.commentary: Metal shipments 105 kt, down 16% YoY on a planned smelter shutdown; CCR volumes 96 kt, down 8%. Record EBITDA of INR918 crore; ex-shutdown EBITDA/t would have been around USD1,000.

segments.name: Novelis
segments.commentary: Shipments 916 kt, down 5% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA USD516 million including an $18 million net positive from Oswego fires and $47 million insurance proceeds. Cost savings run-rate at USD225 million against a USD350-400 million target by FY28 exit; Oswego mill restarted in June.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 sulphuric acid prices expected to stay near Q1 levels; management hopes for no tapering in H2.
Q2 volumes expected higher for both India copper and India downstream aluminium.
India cash cost expected to rise 5-6% QoQ in Q2 on northern-region coal prices during monsoon.
Novelis net leverage expected to fall below 4x, with a level of about 4.5x around end-September; Novelis net debt/EBITDA to start declining in Q4.
Novelis working capital release of USD300-400 million over the next couple of quarters.
Novelis long-term EBITDA/t guidance of USD600 unchanged; Oswego net cash impact seen at about USD600 million after all insurance recoveries.
Consolidated net leverage to remain around 2x; India net debt/EBITDA not expected to change materially as FY27 is a high-capex year.
Aditya refinery and first 180 kt smelter phase commissioning Dec 2027; second phase Dec 2028; meaningful contribution in FY29. Captive coal: Chakla about 1 Mt and Bandha about 0.5 Mt in FY28.
capex_capacity: Aditya alumina refinery and aluminium smelter expansions progressing on track; strategy to double upstream capacity.
Captive coal mines: Chakla, Bandha and Meenakshi under development. Chakla about 1 Mt and Bandha about 0.5 Mt expected in FY28.
Renewables: 470 MW operational; 414 MW solar/wind and 90 MW RE-RTC pumped storage to be added in FY27, taking the portfolio to 884 MW solar/wind/hydel and 125 MW RE-RTC.
Novelis Bay Minette 600 kt greenfield rolling and recycling plant on track for completion in 2026, with initial commissioning underway.
Aditya Battery Foil and Taloja AC Fins commissioned last quarter and in customer qualification; specialty alumina (precipitated hydrate) nearing commercialisation.
Copper smelter expansion, Pakhajan scrap melting project (commissioning this year, IRR in high teens) and copper smelter timing under review, with smelter output expected in FY29.
demand_pricing: LME aluminium moved from about INR3,150/t before the Middle East conflict to a peak near USD3,850/t, then eased to USD3,200/t after the ceasefire; management expects a 2026 deficit of about 1 Mt.
India aluminium demand about 1.5 Mt in Q1 FY27, up about 3% YoY; flat-rolled products up more than 10%; electrical segment weak on deferred contractor-led projects.
Indian refined copper demand 359 kt, down 9% YoY; TC/RC at -26 to -30 cents/lb; concentrate tightness expected to persist through 2026.
Alumina prices around USD330-340/t, slightly up from historic lows, and expected to stay in this range until Middle East smelters return.

Novelis faces US Section 232 tariffs of about USD70 million in Q1 (versus USD24 million last quarter) as it imports metal while Oswego is down; management expects some tariff cost for the next couple of quarters.
Japan/Korea MJP premiums elevated due to Middle East supply disruption; expected to ease next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Novelis tariff impact of USD70 million excludable to show EBITDA/t above USD600, and why did it rise from USD24 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Novelis Steve Fisher said it was not excluded from adjusted EBITDA and advised against adding it back; tariffs stem from importing metal while Oswego is down and will persist for a few quarters. Dev Ahuja said third-party costs sit below the line as fire costs, while own-network imports do not, and declined to give specific guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the brand royalty to Birla Group Holdings affect Hindalco?
qa_highlights.answer: Satish Pai said both Novelis and Hindalco will pay a royalty of 0.25% of revenue to Birla Group Holdings, capped at INR225 crore per year, which is below Hindalco's materiality threshold and does not affect dividend or capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD300/t downstream aluminium EBITDA sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Pai said USD250/t is a more sustainable level for the rest of FY27, with the longer-term aluminium downstream target still above USD300/t; more clarity on total downstream (including copper) is due next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will Novelis leverage fall well below 4x?
qa_highlights.answer: Dev Ahuja said Novelis will be below 4x, helped by insurance recoveries, working capital release, lower ABL borrowings and higher EBITDA run-rate, after about 4.5x at end-September.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Oswego insurance recovery outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Dev Ahuja said cumulative cash impact so far is about USD1.4 billion net of recoveries, of which USD300 million has been recovered; the net cash impact is expected to settle at about USD600 million, with a couple of hundred million possibly slipping into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedging position for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Pai said 21% of FY28 aluminium is hedged at USD3,160/t, with a target of about USD3,200/t; no further FY27 hedging is being added due to deep backwardation.

risks_watch: Novelis tariff costs (USD70 million in Q1) persist until supply chains are reconfigured; cash impact of Oswego fire pending insurance recovery.
India copper concentrate tightness and negative TC/RC keep pressure on smelter economics; copper smelter expansion is capital-intensive.
Elevated coal, sulphur and MJP costs; India cash costs seen rising 5-6% QoQ in Q2.
Related-party royalty (0.25% of revenue, capped at INR225 crore per year) under SEBI LODR disclosure.
USMCA status is uncertain; management does not expect a material impact.
Exceptional items of about INR300 crore at consolidated level (Ind AS vs US GAAP) expected to fall away as Oswego recovers; watch Q2 for confirmation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India upstream and downstream profitability and Novelis recovery, but noticeably evasive on tariff quantification, royalty terms and the consolidated exceptional-item treatment, deferring details offline or to next quarter.
key_quotes: Our quarterly EBITDA was a record INR7,390 crores, up 81% year-on-year.
We view the impact of the outage largely as a timing issue rather than a structural one.
Our long-term EBITDA per ton guidance of $600 remains unchanged.
I would say more around USD250 is a more sustainable number.

Novelis Bay Minette 600 kt greenfield rolling and recycling plant
414 MW solar/wind and 90 MW RE-RTC pumped storage to be added in FY27

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth figure guided; management expects higher Q2 volumes in India copper and downstream aluminium, a 2x-strategy to double upstream capacity, and Novelis cost savings of USD225m run-rate toward USD350-400m by FY28, with Aditya smelter/refinery only live from Dec 2027 and Bay Minette due in 2026.
